evidence.text: Simply Good Foods (Quest/Atkins, the closest listed protein-brand peer) reported on 2026-10-27, after BellRing last spoke. It took a near-double-digit price increase and guided FY27 net sales -13% to -17% and adj EBITDA -9% to -14%. The stock still rose +11.4% because the Q4 beat and the margin reset were read as a floor. That reaction function, a trough-valuation protein name buying a price-led reset, is directly relevant to BRBR's first FY27 guide on a double-digit Premier shake price increase.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: BRBR's own guide lines have been sold. May 2026 -38.8% and Feb 2026 -14.4% on cuts. Aug 2026 was only -1.5% on a third cut, which suggests the guide-cut reaction is wearing out at these levels.
evidence.why_not_priced: The peer read is a three-week-old print on a different subcategory. If the market had fully transferred it, BRBR's implied move would be compressed and the 20-day run-up would be larger than +14% against a 67% drawdown. Instead shorts added 2.4M shares in October.
evidence.independence: SMPL's own 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001702744/000170274426000028/a991_pressreleasexq4x2026.htm) confirms the guide figures. It is the same event, so it counts once.

evidence.text: BellRing's CFO said on the Q3 call that 'the other major player in the RTD space' (fairlife) took a double-digit price increase earlier in 2026. Coca-Cola's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-27) says fairlife grew in Jul-Sep 2026, offsetting the Nigeria divestiture. So the category leader's price increase did not break its demand, which is evidence on the elasticity BRBR will guide on for its own double-digit shake increase (management assumes elasticity slightly above 1).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No BRBR print has turned on an elasticity read. The last price increase predates the baseline history.
evidence.why_not_priced: Coca-Cola does not quantify fairlife growth, and no BRBR preview found links it to BRBR's elasticity assumption. If it were priced, the FY27 consensus would not sit at only +0.7% revenue.
evidence.independence: The BRBR Q3 transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15344863892956160) is the source for fairlife's double-digit increase. Different document, same theme. This is a proxy, not a BRBR number.

evidence.text: Fairlife's $650M Webster, NY plant began a production ramp at a 2026-08-20 ribbon-cutting. It adds 5-6M lbs of milk a day and ~30% capacity, and is expected to be fully operational later in 2026. That puts fresh competitor RTD supply on shelves just as Premier raises shake prices by a double-digit amount in FY27. It is a risk to Premier's share and promo depth in the FY27 guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Competition-driven share loss was the narrative behind the Aug 2025 -32.6% and May 2026 -38.8% prints (securities suit alleges masked share erosion).

evidence.text: The FY27 bar is demanding for a new CEO's first guide. Consensus has EPS $1.31 (+25%) on revenue of only +0.7% (stockanalysis, 2026-11-03). evidence.text: On the Q2 call the CFO framed H2 2026 revenue as about 15% above H1, which is about $119.4M on H1 of $103.8M. So if Q3 beats (about $59.5-60M) and management only reiterates H2, the implied Q4 is about $59.5-60M, below the $62.4M Street Q4. evidence.text: ZIM's CFO said in the Q2 release (19 Aug 2026) that the expected H2 improvement 'would enable our Board of Directors to consider declaring a dividend to shareholders based on our third-quarter results'. At the $4.77 consensus EPS (about $575m of net income, 120.6m shares) and net of the -$22m H1 loss, a ~30% payout is about $1.35-1.45 a share, about 4.7% of spot. On an arb name the dividend is value on top of the $35. A larger payout, at the high end of the policy or on a bigger Q3, adds; a board that withholds or trims it citing the merger agreement subtracts.

evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the CFO flagged it three months ago, and arb holders model it. What the market cannot know is the board's choice of payout ratio, and whether it pays 30% of Q3 alone or of 9-month cumulative income. If the market priced a near-certain ~$1.4 plus a possible Q4 true-up before closing, the arb spread would be narrower than the $5.31 it is.
